 Miles Bridges had 24 points (10-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), ten rebounds, two assists, a steal, three blocks, and two 3-pointers on Friday in loss. 
 While Bridges hasn’t been hitting his 3’s this season, he’s done everything else that he was doing in Charlotte last season. He’s scoring at a decent level, he’s rebounding the ball, and playing solid defense. It hasn’t translated to many wins at this point, but he does give them a good defender at the wing position which they didn’t really have last season. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Miles Bridges accumulated 17 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 Bridges shot just 2-of-10 from three on Monday, but a 5-of-7 night from inside the arc helped salvage something for fantasy managers in the field-goal percentage category. The rebounds and assists were good, but the problem for Bridges is that this is another two-game week for the Suns. And Friday’s matchup with the Nuggets won’t be easy. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Miles Bridges recorded 16 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Warriors. 
 Bridges doubled his point total in the Suns’ season-opening loss in Portland, while also adding solid rebounding and assisting. Bridges may not be the most prolific fantasy option, but as in Charlotte, he’s well-positioned to deliver top-100 value in category leagues. Unfortunately, the Suns only play two games in Week 2, starting with the Thunder on Monday. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Miles Bridges tallied eight points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one steal and one blocked shot in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Making his first official appearance in a Suns uniform, Bridges played 29 minutes in Wednesday’s 41-point defeat. The ankle injury he suffered early in the preseason may have played a role, with the Suns hoping to give Bridges more run to build his stamina. Unfortunately, he did little against the Trail Blazers’ deep reserves in what would be a lost night. As he showed in Charlotte, Bridges can provide solid category-league value, but it remains to be seen if that can carry over to Phoenix. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Miles Bridges (ankle) is out for the rest of Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bulls. 
 Bridges injured his right ankle during the first half of Wednesday’s game, ending his night after logging eight minutes. The veteran forward, whose arrival in Phoenix pushed Collin Gillespie out of the starting lineup, finished with three points, one rebound and one assist. However, Rasheer Fleming started the third quarter instead of Gillespie. Bridges’ injury did not appear serious, and the Suns won’t play their first regular-season game until October 21. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #0 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Hornets have traded Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Suns for Grayson Allen, Royce O’Neale and a 2033 first-round pick. 
 With his draft rights acquired on the night of the 2018 NBA Draft, Bridges has spent his entire NBA career in Charlotte. He appeared in 77 games last season, averaging 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 three-pointers while shooting 46.0 percent from the field and 82.2 percent from the foul line. His trade is the second for the Hornets in less than a week as the franchise charts a new path, with LaMelo Ball having been dealt to the Timberwolves on Wednesday. Bridges missed the entire 2022-23 season due to a (since-resolved) domestic abuse case, but has been a productive player when he’s suited up.. Bridges can provide solid fantasy value when available, but his ceiling will be capped in a lineup that features Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 NBA insider Jake Fischer reports that the Hornets are “expected” to make Miles Bridges available via trade in conjunction with this month’s draft. 
 While there were some rumblings that Bridges could be had for the right price at the February trade deadline, the veteran forward remained in Charlotte. However, that may not be the case this summer, based on Fischer’s reporting. Bridges is going into the final year of his contract, with a $22.8 million cap hit. Regarding the draft, the Hornets currently hold two first-round picks, 14th and 18th overall. Would Bridges plus a pick be an approach for the team to take if they wanted to move up? That will be something to keep an eye on, especially with Charlotte also rumored to be seeking an upgrade at the center position. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 Miles Bridges produced 15 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in the loss to the Magic on Friday. 
 Bridges struggled with his three-point shot in the season-ending loss. However, his success inside the arc and at the charity stripe helped him finish as Charlotte’s second-leading scorer on the evening. Bridges didn’t contribute in many other areas, however, and a bad team performance prevented this contest from being competitive through the final horn. He ends his seventh NBA season with averages of 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. His fantasy production slipped this season, as did his overall numbers. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 Miles Bridges added 28 points (10-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal, three blocks and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Heat. 
 Bridges was exceptional on both ends of the floor during Tuesday’s contest. In his team-high 43 minutes, he did lots of damage from beyond the arc, but also had his share of buckets inside the three-point line. The veteran forward also battled on the glass and nearly amassed a double-double. But perhaps his biggest moment came in the closing moments of the game when he went up and blocked Davion Mitchell’s game-winning shot attempt to keep the Hornets’ season alive. Bridges totaled four stocks and will try to land another impactful two-way performance on Friday against the winner of Sixers-Magic. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 Miles Bridges had 25 points (10-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Timberwolves. 
 Bridges has now scored 25 points in two of his last three games and at least 19 points in four consecutive games. The 28-year-old small forward stepped up for the Hornets on a night when Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller combined for just 18 points. Bridges has provided eighth-round per game value over the last two weeks. The Hornets have three games in the last week of the regular season, starting with a matchup against the Celtics on Tuesday.

 Charles Bassey recorded 19 points (7-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds and one assist in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 While Bassey scored nine points in the first half, his role in the Warriors’ rotation grew more important in the second half. Draymond Green was ejected two minutes into the third quarter, giving Bassey more minutes. In 15 second-half minutes, he accumulated 10 points, six rebounds and one assist. Bassey’s 19 points are a career high, and more nights like this would go a long way toward making his contract fully guaranteed come January 10.

 Brandin Podziemski recorded 20 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 Podziemski recorded his second 20-point game of the season on Monday, finishing one point shy of his high (21 vs. the Lakers on Friday). Like Stephen Curry, Podz was most effective during the third quarter, scoring 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting from the field. The negative for fantasy managers is that Podziemski didn’t provide much value beyond the points and three-pointers. They’ll hope for more on Thursday when the Warriors host the Heat.

 Stephen Curry tallied 34 points (9-of-21 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 While he didn’t have his best night shooting the basketball, Curry extended his streak of games with at least 31 points to three. The Warriors star was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 6-of-9 from the field and scoring 18 points. Outside that period, the Suns kept Curry in check, but he still went home with a stat line that many fantasy managers will take without hesitation.

 Austin Reaves lit up the Heat with 27 points (10-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, four three-pointers and five turnovers on Monday.
 The last few games had been rough for Reaves, but he was able to get back on track in this one. The turnovers still weren’t great, and he now has 24 over his last four outings. However, he was far more efficient as a scorer, which helped the Lakers secure a second win in as many days. Reaves has been a high-level second option behind Luka Dončić this season, though the turnovers need to be cleaned up for him to match his production from last year.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday.
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Kessler has finally started dominating the glass. He has recorded three straight double-doubles and has at least 15 points and 15 rebounds in each of his last two outings. Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers have needed, and it has worked out well for fantasy managers as well. With Luka Dončić running the offense, Kessler should continue to be a fantasy star.

 While Mitchell had a spectacular game, volume was an issue. He didn’t miss a shot from the floor, but he only took five shots. Mitchell has had an excellent start to the year, but his lack of shot attempts prevented him from having a better night. However, he continues to dish out the dimes at a high rate, which has been the driving factor behind his top-75 value to start this season.
